text: Habiba Ghribi (Arabic: حبيبة الغريبي), born on 9 April 1984, is a Tunisian middle- and long-distance runner who specialises in the 3000 metres steeplechase. She won the gold medal at the 2012 Summer Olympics, securing Tunisia's first Olympic medal by a woman. She holds the Tunisian national record in the event, set at 9:05.36 during a race at the Memorial van Damme in Brussels on September 2015. Ghribi competed in the IAAF World Cross Country Championships multiple times, winning a silver medal in the steeplechase at the 2006 African Championships in Athletics and a bronze in the 1500 metres at the 2009 Mediterranean Games. She represented Tunisia at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, finishing 13th in the first-ever women's Olympic steeplechase race. At the 2016 Müller Anniversary Games, she won the women's 3000m steeplechase. In 2009, she was voted the Best Sportswoman of the year by the Arabic daily newspaper Assahafa. Ghribi began her career as a cross country runner, competing in the junior race at the 2000 IAAF World Cross Country Championships at age 15, finishing 46th (second best on the Tunisian team), and later placing 76th in the senior short race in 2002. At the 2002 African Championships in Radès, Tunisia, she finished 11th in the 5000 metres final. She won gold in the junior race at the 2002 Pan Arab Cross Country Championships and improved to 23rd in the junior race at the 2003 IAAF World Cross Country Championships, leading Tunisia to 7th place overall. After modest finishes in the World Cross Country short race in 2004 and 2005, she shifted focus to the 3000m steeplechase when it became a world championship event. At the 2005 Helsinki World Championships, she finished eighth in her heat, failing to qualify for the final but setting a personal best and Tunisian record of 9:51.49. The following year, she won silver at the 2006 African Championships behind world medallist Jeruto Kiptum. At the 2008 Beijing Olympics, she improved her record to 9:25.50 in the heats but finished 13th in the final. In 2009, she competed in the IAAF World Cross Country Championships, finishing 41st, and ran the 1500 metres at the Mediterranean Games, achieving a personal best of 4:12.37 and earning a bronze medal. At the 2009 World Championships in Athletics, she placed sixth with a time of 9:12.52, improving her best significantly. She failed to finish the 2009 IAAF World Athletics Final. In recognition of her 2009 achievements, she was named "Best Sportswoman in 2009" by Assahafa. In September 2015, she ran a personal best, Tunisian national record, African record, and the fourth-fastest time ever at 9:05.36 in Brussels. In June 2016, Ghribi was officially named the 2012 Olympic champion in the women's 3000m steeplechase after original gold medalist Yuliya Zaripova of Russia was disqualified due to a doping violation. As of December 2016, Ghribi was considering legal action to recover at least $38,000 in prize money that Zaripova had received from events where she was later disqualified. Ghribi married her coach, Khaled Boudhraa, of Algerian origin, and announced her divorce after the London Olympics. She later got engaged to athlete Bouabdellah Tahri and, on September 30, 2017, married Yassine Saya, a Tunisian businessman. She gave birth to a daughter, Alyssa, on May 2, 2019, in Canada.
